newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli dollar-linked bonds soar on strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli dollar-linked bonds soar on strong dollar.

text.p: Prices of Israeli dollar-linked bonds soared on Tuesday in stormy trading affected by the fall of the shekel against the dollar, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.2 pct to 107.7
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.34 pct at 107.43
* Unlinked government bonds: -0.28 pct to 108.84
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +1.97 pct to 108.64
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: -0.12 pct to 107.01
Volume including Makams was 161 million shekels, including a medium volume of 12.8 million shekels for dollar-linked bonds.
"The events in the foreign exchange market affected trading in all the bonds," said Adam Reuter, managing director of Financial Immunities consultancy.

"There was an enormous demand - 266 million dollars, without supply - for dollar-linked bonds because of the strenghtening of the dollar against the shekel yesterday and today. Prices of short-term CPI-linked bonds rose as well, against sharp losses of unlinked bonds, on fears that the dollar exchange rate will boost inflation," he said.

The shekel declined against the dollar for the third consecutive session on Tuesday. At its nadir on Tuesday, the shekel was trading at 3.55 shekels to the dollar, against 3.484 on Monday and 3.419 last Thursday. The currency's representative rate was set on Tuesday at 3.5060.
Yields on dollar linked bonds fell to around 4.6 percent from around 5.6 on Monday, traders said.
Reuter added that prices of CPI-linked medium and long bonds had posted small losses on fears that interest rates would go up in future.

After last week's interest rate cut, yields on long CPI-linked bonds fell below four percent. On Tuesday yields of these bonds rose to about 4.13 percent, while yields of CPI-linked short bonds fell to 4.6 percent from 4.66 percent on Monday.

After the Israeli cabinet adopted a plan on Wednesday to widen the exchange rate band and adjust its diagonal rate, the central bank lowered its key lending rate 1.2 percentage points to an annualised 12.7 percent.

The bond market was unaffected by worries about the imminent appointment of Ariel Sharon as finance minister, a trader said. These worries and concerns about interest rates caused shares to fall sharply in early trading on Tuesday.
"Today the exchange rate of the dollar was the only thing that affected trading," said a trader at Israel Discount Bank.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.5 shekels)
